1.explanation:
1. src/ol/MapBrowserEventHandler.js – this module was updated in v6.4.0 to throttle pointer events via requestAnimationFrame and to perform additional checks before firing pointermove. The new logic introduces extra per‐frame overhead.

2. src/ol/PluggableMap.js – the public forEachFeatureAtPixel API used by typical pointermove handlers now delegates deeper into the renderer on each event, and changes here can multiply the cost of every hit test.

3. src/ol/render/canvas/hitdetect.js – this file implements the low‐level hit‐detection used by canvas vector layers. Any changes here (for example to geometry intersection tests or caching) will directly affect the speed of feature lookup during pointermove.

4. src/ol/renderer/canvas/VectorLayer.js – this renderer invokes the hitdetect routines and manages style function calls. Since our demo uses non‐cached styles, every pointermove triggers fresh style computations and image lookups here, making the slowdown more pronounced after the v6.4.0 restructuring.
1.bug_scenario: In our app upgrading from OL v6.3.1 to v6.4.0 causes “pointermove”‐driven interactions (like cursor changes on feature hover, pan, zoom, etc.) to become noticeably sluggish when many styled vector features are on the map. In the supplied GIFs you can see that moving the cursor over 1000 circle features fires a pointermove listener which in v6.3.1 updates the cursor almost instantly, but in v6.4.0 the same listener lags significantly behind the mouse. The regression is due to internal changes to how pointermove events are throttled and how hit–detection and style lookups are performed on each move.

2.explanation:
• MapBrowserEventHandler.js sets up and dispatches all low‐level pointer events.  In 6.4.0 its pointermove path now walks through every feature on each move, triggering hit detection and style evaluation.  
• interaction/Pointer.js drives the high‐level pointermove callback logic – it now ends up calling into style and hit‐testing routines far more often than before.  
• layer/Vector.js contains the vector hit‐testing code that loops over every feature and invokes the style function on each one; with uncached styles it recomputes symbolizers repeatedly.  
• style/IconImageCache.js used to cache icon images effectively.  A change in 6.4.0 prevents reuse of previously built images for dynamic styles, forcing repeated image construction on every move.  
Together these changes make pointermove handling much heavier and explain the observed slowdown in 6.4.0 versus 6.3.1.
2.bug_scenario: In 6.4.0 the handling of “pointermove” has become dramatically slower when you have many (e.g. 1000) features with uncached styles.  On every mouse‐move the library now reconstructs or re‐evaluates styles, re‐runs hit detection over all of the vector features, and recreates icon images instead of hitting previously built caches.  The net result is that moving the cursor (or panning/zooming) feels sluggish compared to 6.3.1, where style evaluation and icon image lookup were cached more aggressively.
